newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Achmea 1996 earnings 21.5 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Achmea 1996 earnings 21.5 pct higher.

text.p: Dutch insurance and banking group Achmea said on Friday its 1996 net profit rose by 21.5 percent to 572 million guilders.
"For 1997 we expect a further increase in turnover and profits," chairman Gijs Swalef told a news conference on the group's 1996 results.
Swalef said the group was aiming to expand its business in the Benelux (Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg) in 1997.
Total premium income of the Achmea insurance companies rose by 6.2 percent to 10.3 billion guilders in 1996.
Gross premium income of the life and pension insurance companies, including single-premium business, increased by 11.7 percent to 2.8 billion guilders.
In non-life gross premium income rose 5.1 percent to over 2.0 billion guilders, while health insurance premium income grew by 3.9 percent to 5.4 billion guilders.
Income from banking services, including mortgages, was two percent higher at 1.1 billion guilders, Achmea said, adding that pre-tax profits in this sector rose by 34.4 percent to 82 million guilders.

"During the year (1996), the extension of Achmea's home market to cover the Benelux led to further investments at CB Direct in Brussels, which secured a growing share of the Belgian insurance market by direct sales of motor insurance," Achmea said in a statement.
"At Achmea's subsidiary, Banque Colbert in Luxembourg, expansion into asset-protection products and life insurance is under consideration," Achmea said.
"We are aiming to increase our banking activities," said Swalef, adding there were not many possibilities for an aqcuisitions in the Netherlands.
"But, we are looking for possibilities in Belgium," he said.
Pre-tax results from the group's life insurance activities rose by 10.8 percent in 1996 to 317 million guilders.
Non-life pre-tax profits were 7.8 percent higher at 111 million guilders.
Health insurance activities posted an 6.9 percent higher pre-tax profit at 170 million guilders.
Swalef said the group's motor insurance activities were close to break-even, but he added that this segment would never become a goldmine.

Achmea Holding is part of Eureko, a pan-European group of listed and unlisted insurers. Beside Achmea the group exists of Britain's Friends Provident, German Gothaer Versicherungen, Sweden's Wasa, Topdanmark of Denmark and BCP of Portugal.
